newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends little changed vs US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends little changed vs US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan ended little changed at 8.2950 against the U.S. dollar on Monday in Shanghai from a seven-week high of 8.2949 last Friday with trading most active around the key 8.2950 resistance level, traders said.
The weighted average price on Friday was 8.2951.
Dealers said the yuan was supported by pro-yuan sentiment but its topside was capped by selling from traders fearful of intervention from the central bank.
The yuan opened at 8.2950 and moved around the opening level for most of the session, hitting a temporary intraday high of 8.2898 and a low of 8.3023.
Trading was dull early in the session but picked up later with the underlying strong yuan trend still much in evidence.

"Active buying is expected to push the yuan above the 8.2950 again, although there was good selling today which stopped it," said one dealer. "Worries about the central bank depressing the yuan was the main negative factor."
He said he expected the yuan to move around 8.2950 again on Tuesday.
The yuan closed down at an intraday low of 6.6493 from 6.6380 against 100 Japanese yen and unchanged at an intraday high of 1.0700 against the Hong Kong dollar.
